correctness.rationale: For real 1<p<∞ let q=p/(p−1), project every x∈R² onto fixed Euclidean closed unit disk in ambient ℓp metric. Strict convexity yields uniqueness; exterior KKT gives x=y+s J_q(y), y on Euclidean unit circle, s>0. Differentiating normal coordinates produces rank-one tangential derivative with operator norm ||v||_p||J_q(y)||_q divided by |y_1|^q+|y_2|^q+s(q−1)(|y_1|^(q−2)|y_2|^q+|y_1|^q|y_2|^(q−2)). Denominator increases with s; letting s→0 and writing t=|y_2/y_1| yields claimed one-variable supremum. Integrating local bounds over line segments split at disk boundary/coordinate axes gives the global bound; exterior near-boundary tangent derivatives give matching lower bound. For p=4, z=t^(4/9), u=z+1/z, exact fourth-power ratio (u³−3u−1)/(u−1)³ maximized at u=1+sqrt3 to give 1+2/sqrt3. Small-t exponent comparison proves strict amplification for all p≠2; p=2 recovers Hilbert nonexpansivity. Scope excludes p=1,∞ and dimensions beyond two.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader all-planar-cone theorem covers wedges (straight rays), not the *Euclidean disk* as target. The Lorentz cone model likewise has straight boundary rays in the plane. Jinlu Li (2024) studies radial projection onto balls of the same Banach norm, while the assigned Euclidean disk is not an ℓp ball when p≠2. The probability-simplex limit constant 1+2/sqrt3 occurs for a different polyhedral target in variable dimensions.
